name: Should landlords hire one general contractor or manage separate trade subcontractors?

mainEntity.name: Should landlords hire one general contractor or manage separate trade subcontractors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring a single general contractor is generally far more cost-effective and faster than managing separate subcontractors yourself. Managing individual drywallers, painters, tile setters, plumbers, and carpenters requires substantial time, and scheduling delays between independent trades quickly extend vacancy periods. As an owner-operated contractor, Abraham Becerra acts as the primary contact and on-site lead, directing his in-house team on framing, drywall, tile, and trim while coordinating mechanical trades. This unified management keeps your turnover schedule on track and avoids miscommunication between trades.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hiring one general contractor keeps schedules tight and avoids costly vacancy gaps caused by managing independent trades yourself.
